intent_signal: informational / research — pre-trip planning. Searcher is comparing destination camps (usually for a 2-week to 3-month trip) and wants to understand the landscape before committing. Sub-segment planning 3+ months with long-stay visa intent.
common_ground: All listicles include Tiger Muay Thai (Phuket) as a reference point — the category anchor brand
Phuket (Tiger, Sinbi, Rawai camps) dominates content — Chiang Mai underrepresented
Most lists cover 5-10 camps, sorted by location/city
Budget context is thin: day rates or vague USD monthly ranges, no THB specifics
DTV visa is mentioned by at most 1-2 articles, never as a decision-making filter

gap.description: No listicle frames 'best camp' from a beginner + long-stay + visa angle. All current SERP results are either commercial camp pages (Tiger, Sinbi, Santai promoting themselves) or generic listicles without DTV context. Nobody tells the searcher: 'if you want to stay 3+ months, your camp choice IS your visa strategy — here's how to pick.' The Chiang Mai family-camp angle (affordable, open-air, non-intimidating, DTV support) is entirely absent from top results. No article uses DTV eligibility as a camp-selection criterion. No honest 'we're not Tiger Muay Thai but here's why Chiang Mai might be better for you' take exists.

weakness: All camp-authored listicles are self-promotional — searchers know this, which is why Reddit outperforms them for trust
Chiang Mai camps receive 1-2 brief mentions in Phuket-dominated listicles despite being cheaper and more beginner-friendly
No article addresses 'all-inclusive with DTV support' as a camp feature
Pricing transparency across the SERP is poor — THB prices for all-inclusive packages are absent
No article addresses women/family/non-fighter personas directly
Freshness: most listicles are updated annually but training costs and visa rules shift more frequently
recommended_angle: Position Wildcat's article as the honest 'which Thailand camp is right for YOU?' guide — structured by traveler type (beginner, long-stayer, woman, fighter), with Chiang Mai vs Phuket vs Bangkok as a key decision axis, real THB price comparisons, and a dedicated 'DTV consideration' section that no competitor includes. Wildcat is listed honestly alongside Tiger/Sinbi/Santai (not #1) but earns the 'family camp + DTV support, Chiang Mai' slot no competitor currently occupies.
